definitions: The principle that each state has exclusive authority over its territory and internal affairs, free from external interference.
The supreme, absolute, and uncontrollable power by which an independent state is governed and from which all specific political powers are derived.
examples: The United Nations Charter upholds the principle of state sovereignty.
Interference in another nation's internal affairs can be seen as a violation of state sovereignty.
Many international laws are built upon the foundation of state sovereignty.
